newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Troops sent to protect Ecuador Congress.
newsitem.headline: Troops sent to protect Ecuador Congress.

text.p: Soldiers took up positions around Ecuador's Congress on Wednesday and their commanding officer said they had been sent to protect legislators.

"We have come by order of the armed forces' joint-chiefs of staff to provide security for Congress and stop mobs entering the Congress," Lt. Col. Victor Torres told reporters. "The objective of preventing mobs from entering Congress is to allow the legislators to act free of pressure," he said.
Witnesses said about 150 armed soldiers in combat uniform surrounded the Congress.
The action took place as trade unions who started a 48-hour general strike on Wednesday planned to march on Congress to demand the resignation of President Abdala Bucaram.
Congress Speaker Fabian Alarcon was meeting with top party leaders to discuss calling a session of Congress to depose the president.

Alarcon told reporters he had received threats to dissolve Congress if the session went ahead. While Alarcon did not say who made the threats, a senior congressional source told Reuters that Bucaram had threatened the speaker.

Ecuador, an Andean country of 11.7 million people, has been gripped by social unrest since Bucaram's government imposed tough austerity measures and drastically boosted the price of public services in January.
